newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt denies Mubarak-Weizman meeting planned.
newsitem.headline: Egypt denies Mubarak-Weizman meeting planned.

text.p: Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa on Thursday denied reports that President Hosni Mubarak and Israeli President Ezer Weizman planned to meet soon to break the crisis in the Israeli-Palestinian peace process.
"President Mubarak called President Weizman yesterday within the framework of contacts agreed upon. There is no meeting between the two presidents during the next few days," Moussa told reporters.

Weizman, an architect of Israel's landmark peace treaty with Egypt while a cabinet minister in 1979, told reporters in Israel that Mubarak proposed in the phone call on Wednesday that they meet in Egypt. An aide to Weizman said they expected a meeting soon.

"I view this as another attempt to break some ice...It's important to all of us that the whole political process begin to move again. Will it move by way of President Mubarak or not? I don't know," Weizman said.

Moussa was speaking after his second round of talks with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in as many days on ways to rescue peace talks that have been stalled since Israel began building a settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18.
